one_liner: UNESCO Portuguese port city of Mazagan and the Mazagan Beach resort strip, ~90 km down the Atlantic coast from Casablanca.
brief: El Jadida is a major port city on Morocco's Atlantic coast, 90–96 km southwest of Casablanca in the Casablanca-Settat region. Its historic core, the Portuguese City of Mazagan, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2004) — a 16th-century fortified colony famous for its star-shaped ramparts and the vaulted Portuguese Cistern. The city pairs this heritage draw with a working fishing and commercial port beneath the citadel and a long resort corniche. Just north toward Casablanca sits the Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort at El Haouzia, one of the country's largest integrated beach resorts (casino, golf, marina-side leisure). El Jadida sits on the direct Casablanca–Marrakech rail and road axis, making it a high-demand summer-leisure and weekend-escape destination for the Casablanca metro. On the water, El Jadida is a natural southern anchor of the Casablanca coastal cluster: a Casablanca ⇄ El Jadida marine shuttle (~57 nm) offers a congestion-free premium alternative to the saturated coastal road, and the Mazagan resort marina is a distinct high-value transfer node.
